name: Zazen / zuochan (seated meditation)
method_summary: Sitting upright in full or half lotus on a cushion, hands in the cosmic mudrā (left on right, thumbs touching), eyes half-open, breathing naturally through the nose, letting go of involvements; in the Platform Sūtra's redefinition, 'sitting' is thoughts not arising toward objects and 'meditation' is seeing the unmoving self-nature. In Sōtō it is just sitting; in Rinzai the seat of kōan work.

warnings.text: Fixing the mind and viewing stillness is a sickness, not meditation; long sitting constrains the body without benefit.
Sitting with an empty mind falls into indeterminate emptiness.
Taking quiet as the ultimate is to be captured by heretical silent-illumination Chan (Dahui).

equivalents.note: Chan redefines seated meditation so as not to be a pursuit of absorption states.

name: Shikantaza (just sitting)
method_summary: Sitting wholeheartedly with no object, method or goal beyond the sitting itself — 'thinking of not-thinking: non-thinking'; understood as the enactment of original realization rather than a means to it.

warnings.text: Do not seek realization apart from practice (Bendōwa).

name: Silent illumination (mozhao)
method_summary: Sitting in silence in which words are forgotten while the mind's illumination remains clear, 'knowing without touching things, illumining without facing objects'; silence and illumination must be kept together.

warnings.text: If illumination loses silence, aggression appears; if silence loses illumination, it becomes murky superfluous dharma (Hongzhi).
Dahui warns that 'silent illumination' taught as becoming cold ash and dead wood cuts off buddha-wisdom.

name: Kōan introspection (sanzen, kōan practice)
method_summary: Working on an assigned kōan in zazen and daily activity, presenting one's understanding to the teacher in private interview; after the first barrier (e.g. 'wu', the sound of one hand), a graded series of cases, capping phrases and verses deepens and tests insight.

warnings.text: Do not seek the meaning in the phrase or understand it by reasoning (Yuanwu; Dahui).
Bankei held that manufacturing doubt trades the buddha-mind for a doubt.

name: Huatou / hwadu (observing the critical phrase)
method_summary: Pressing down all discriminating mind and holding the key word of a case (e.g. 'wu') with doubt at every moment and in every posture, without interpreting it, until the doubt shatters.

warnings.text: Eight things to avoid: understanding it as being or non-being, by reasoning, by deliberation, in gestures, in words, sinking into no-concern, accepting it where raised, seeking proof in texts (Dahui).
Do not wait for awakening: 'if you keep your mind on the breaking, it will never break' (Dahui).

prerequisites: great faith, great doubt, great determination (Gaofeng)

name: Turning the light around (huiguang fanzhao / hoegwang banjo)
method_summary: Turning awareness back from its objects to its source — asking who it is that sees, hears and asks, or listening back to the hearing-nature — so as to recognise the empty and calm numinous awareness.

name: Awareness of arising thoughts
method_summary: 'When a thought arises, be aware of it; when aware of it, it vanishes'; 'do not fear thoughts arising, only fear being slow to notice'.

warnings.text: Wumen lists 'being aware of thoughts as they arise' among Chan faults ('toying with spirits') when taken as an end.

name: Ten methods of practising no-mind
method_summary: Ten alternative methods (awareness, resting, extinguishing mind or objects or both, keeping both, whole substance, whole function, substance-is-function, transcending both) of which one suffices, chosen by affinity.

name: Wall-gazing (biguan)
method_summary: Bodhidharma's 'abiding firmly in wall-gazing' in which self and other, ordinary and holy are one; in the tradition, his nine years sitting facing a wall at Shaolin.

name: The four practices of Bodhidharma
method_summary: Requiting enmity (accepting suffering as past karma), according with conditions, seeking nothing, and according with the Dharma.

name: Guarding the mind (shouxin)
method_summary: Guarding the original true mind so that deluded thoughts do not arise and the sense of 'mine' ceases; with Daoxin's 'guarding the one without moving'.

warnings.text: The Platform Sūtra rejects 'viewing the mind' and 'viewing purity' as binding oneself with purity.

name: One-practice samādhi (yixing sanmei)
method_summary: In the Platform Sūtra: always practising a straight mind in walking, standing, sitting and lying, not sitting motionless.

warnings.text: Taking it as sitting without moving and suppressing thoughts makes one like an insentient thing and obstructs the Way.

name: Formless precepts and threefold refuge
method_summary: Huineng's ceremony at the Dafan temple: the formless repentance, the four great vows, the formless threefold refuge in awakening, rightness and purity, and refuge in the three bodies of one's own nature.

name: Formless repentance
method_summary: Resolving in past, present and future thoughts not to be stained by foolishness, deceit or jealousy; confessing past faults and resolving not to repeat them; the sin that cannot be found is absolved (Huike and Sengcan).

name: The four great vows (inward form)
method_summary: Vowing to save the beings of one's own mind, cut off its afflictions, learn the Dharma gates of one's own nature and accomplish its buddha-way; chanted daily in Zen monasteries.

name: Samu / puqing (communal work)
method_summary: Manual labour shared by the whole community, high and low, as practice; 'a day without work, a day without food'; the cook's work done with joyful, nurturing and great mind.

name: Monastic life under the pure rules
method_summary: Daily and annual rhythm of the Chan/Zen monastery: morning and evening assemblies, sitting in the Sangha hall by seniority, formal meals, sūtra chanting, work, retreats and ceremonies.

name: Kinhin (walking meditation)
method_summary: Walking slowly (Sōtō) or briskly (Rinzai) in line between periods of sitting, keeping the posture and attention of zazen.

name: Shouts and blows (he, bang)
method_summary: The teacher's shout or strike used to cut off conceptual thinking and test the student in encounter; Linji's four kinds of shout.

warnings.text: Dahui warns against imitating dramatic acts as 'wondrous function' without insight.

name: Naikan (introspection) of Hakuin
method_summary: A cure for Zen sickness: lying on the back with legs stretched, one gathers breath and energy into the lower abdomen (tanden, kikai) and soles, contemplating that this field is one's original face, Pure Land and Amitābha; the heat of the upper body descends and health returns. (Summary only.)

warnings.text: Hakuin presents it as a remedy for illness caused by unbalanced striving, to restore health so that practice can continue — not as a goal.

name: Nanso no hō (the soft-butter method)
method_summary: Visualising a lump of fragrant soft butter on the crown that melts and flows down through the whole body, washing away illness and pain. (Summary only.)

warnings.text: Given as a healing method for Zen sickness in the Yasenkanna.

name: Nenbutsu Zen (joint practice of Chan and recitation)
method_summary: Reciting Amitābha's name as a Chan practice, sometimes with the critical phrase 'who is it that recites the Buddha's name?'; advocated by Yongming Yanshou, Zhongfeng Mingben, Yunqi Zhuhong and the Ōbaku school; the Platform Sūtra holds that the awakened purify their own minds instead.

warnings.text: The deluded recite the Buddha's name seeking birth in the West; the awakened purify their own minds (Platform Sūtra); joint practice was later debated (dsp:chan-and-nianfo).

name: Drawn-out recitation of the Buddha's name (Jingzhong)
method_summary: In Musang's assemblies, reciting the Buddha's name with a drawn-out voice to the end of a breath, then stopping thought, before the teaching of no-remembering, no-thinking, no-forgetting.

name: Long sitting without lying down (changzuo buwo / jangjwa bulwa)
method_summary: Sitting day and night without lying down for long periods; reported of Northern-school practice and kept by some Korean Seon practitioners.

warnings.text: 'Long sitting constrains the body — what benefit to the principle?' (Huineng); Jinul lists 'always sitting and never lying down' among austerities useless without knowing one's own mind.

name: Sesshin (intensive retreat)
method_summary: Periods (usually seven days) of intensive zazen, interviews and talks in silence, e.g. the rōhatsu sesshin ending on 8 December for the Buddha's awakening.

name: Dokusan / sanzen (private interview)
method_summary: Private meeting with the teacher to present one's understanding of the kōan or to receive guidance.

name: Susokukan (counting the breath)
method_summary: Counting exhalations from one to ten as a beginner's method of settling in zazen.
notes: Common in modern Zen instruction; classical sources not identified in this pass.

name: Sūtra and dhāraṇī chanting in Zen liturgy
method_summary: Daily chanting of the Heart Sūtra, dhāraṇīs (e.g. the Great Compassion Dhāraṇī), the Sandōkai and Hōkyō zanmai (Sōtō), Hakuin's Zazen wasan (Rinzai), and dedications of merit; Ōbaku chants in Ming Chinese pronunciation.

name: Ōryōki (formal monastic meal)
method_summary: Eating with nested bowls in a prescribed sequence of offering, chanting and cleaning, as practice (Dōgen's Fushukuhanpō).

name: Takuhatsu (alms round)
method_summary: Mendicant alms-rounds in which monks receive offerings, practising humility and giving donors merit.

name: Jukai (receiving the precepts)
method_summary: Ceremony of receiving the bodhisattva precepts (in Sōtō the sixteen: three refuges, three pure precepts, ten grave precepts) with a lineage chart (kechimyaku).

name: Niō Zen (guardian-king Zen)
method_summary: Suzuki Shōsan's practice of sitting and working with the fierce energy of the temple guardian kings, with contemplation of death.

name: Suizen (blowing Zen)
method_summary: Playing the shakuhachi as meditation by Fuke-school komusō.

name: Abiding in the Unborn
method_summary: Bankei's teaching: without special practice or kōan struggle, simply do not turn the unborn buddha-mind into anger, desire or thought.
